description: The OrionX is an engineering team dedicated to developing innovative solutions in the fields of space exploration and satellite systems. Drawing inspiration from the constellation Orion, our team aims to create sustainable and practical solutions focused on control systems, data streams, and space research technologies.
summary: SPHEREx Sky Tracker is an open-access, web-based astronomical discovery platform designed to transform NASA’s massive 102-band SPHEREx infrared data and multi-epoch NASA/IPAC Infrared Science Archive (IRSA) catalogs (WISE/NEOWISE and 2MASS) into a fast, scientifically accurate browser tool. Addressing the challenge of processing and cross-matching complex space observation archives, our platform allows users to query celestial coordinates or specific targets—such as high-proper-motion stars and brown dwarfs (WISE 0855, Barnard's Star, Epsilon Indi B) or variable stars (RW Aurigae, R Draconis)—within seconds. The system automatically fetches multi-epoch FITS image cutouts, tracks astrometric proper motion across time, and generates interactive photometric light curves and spectral analyses. By making complex infrared observations effortlessly accessible without heavy desktop software, SPHEREx Sky Tracker empowers both professional researchers and citizen scientists to explore dynamic cosmic changes and moving celestial objects on a unified standard platform.

QUICK ACCESS LINKS • Live Web Application: https://spherex-izleyici.onrender.com • GitHub Source Repository: https://github.com/Kaanerkn/spherex-izleyici • 7-Slide Presentation Deck: https://github.com/Kaanerkn/spherex-izleyici/blob/main/The-ORIONx-Demo.pdf
1. OVERVIEW: WHAT DOES IT DO & WHY DOES IT MATTER? SPHEREx scans the entire sky approximately every six months across 102 near-infrared spectral bands, generating imaging and spectral data for over one billion celestial objects. Manually downloading and inspecting raw multi-gigabyte FITS files across multiple epochs is practically impossible for most users.
SPHEREx Sky Tracker (developed by Team THE ORIONx) transforms this massive infrared dataset—alongside archival data from NASA IRSA—into a fast, open-access web discovery platform. It allows both professional researchers and citizen scientists to search any sky coordinate or target and analyze positional shifts (astrometry) and brightness variations (photometry/spectroscopy) within seconds directly in their browser.
2. HOW IT WORKS: SCIENTIFIC & TECHNICAL WORKFLOW • Why Infrared & 102 Bands: Extremely cold celestial objects—such as brown dwarfs, Y-dwarfs, and hypothetical outer solar system bodies (Planet X)—barely emit visible light according to Planck's black-body radiation law, radiating almost exclusively in the infrared. Furthermore, 102 spectral bands mean each pixel carries a 102-point energy spectrum rather than a simple color image, revealing distinct absorption lines for water (H2O), methane (CH4), and carbon monoxide (CO).
• Capturing Dynamic Changes Over Time: 1) Positional Change (Astrometry): Detects angular shifts of nearby celestial objects caused by their intrinsic velocity (proper motion) and the 6-month orbital perspective shift of Earth around the Sun (parallax). 2) Brightness Change (Photometry): Tracks luminosity variations over 6-month intervals caused by stellar pulsations, internal instabilities, or circumstellar dust disks.
• Data Pipeline (From Search to Evidence): When a user queries a target or coordinate, our modular backend queries NASA/IPAC Infrared Science Archive (IRSA), SIMBAD, MOST, and JPL Horizons. Through selective FITS reading and scientific processing, it extracts multi-epoch cutouts, cross-matches catalog positions, calculates trajectories and light curves, and streams interactive visualizations to the browser in real time.
3. FIVE LIVE BENCHMARK EVIDENCES IN OUR DEMO To validate our platform's scientific claims, we integrated five distinct benchmark targets into the live demo:
• RW Aurigae: Young T Tauri variable star and planet-forming disk system demonstrating circumstellar brightness changes.
• Barnard's Star: The second closest star system to our Solar System, showcasing extreme proper motion across epochs.
• WISE 0855 ↔ Luhman 16: The coldest known Y-dwarf and the closest brown dwarf binary system, proving infrared detection of ultra-cold bodies.
• R Draconis: Mira-type pulsating variable star whose infrared brightness changes significantly over time.
• Epsilon Indi B: Brown dwarf companion orbiting a Sun-like star, highlighting sub-stellar trajectory and spectral tracking.
4. TOOLS, CODING LANGUAGES & SOFTWARE ARCHITECTURE
• Backend: Python, modular scientific processing pipeline, astronomical FITS & WCS parsing (Astropy/NumPy), automated pytest test suite, and upstream configuration management (TOML).
• Frontend: React, TypeScript, HTML5/CSS3, interactive multi-epoch sky/cutout visualizers, and real-time photometric/spectral charting.
• Astronomical Data & APIs: NASA IRSA (SPHEREx, WISE/NEOWISE, 2MASS), CDS SIMBAD, MOST (Moving Object Search Tool), and NASA JPL Horizons.
• DevOps & Deployment: Docker containerization (Dockerfile), Render cloud platform (render.yaml), and Git/GitHub version control.
5. CREATIVITY, ETHICAL RIGOR & INTENDED IMPACT
• Scientific Honesty (Candidate Flagging): A crucial factor our team considered is scientific integrity. Anomalous detections or moving sources that do not match existing catalogs are never falsely sensationalized as "confirmed new discoveries"; instead, our algorithm classifies and presents them transparently as "unmatched candidates" with full source provenance for further verification.
• Selective Reading Architecture: Rather than forcing users to download heavy astronomical software (like SAOImage DS9) or massive FITS tables, our selective reading pipeline fetches only the required spatial/spectral slices, reducing analysis time from hours to seconds.
• Bilingual & Inclusive Design: Featuring both English and Turkish interfaces, one-click data export capabilities, and complete source transparency, SPHEREx Sky Tracker bridges the gap between professional astrophysics and citizen science, establishing a standard platform for exploring the dynamic infrared universe.
6. ACKNOWLEDGEMENT OF SUPER INTELLIGENCE (AI) USE
Large Language Models (LLMs) were utilized during development for technical research/information gathering and Python/TypeScript debugging and troubleshooting. All scientific pipelines, NASA IRSA data integrations, astronomical validations, and documentation/translations were authored and verified by Team THE ORIONx.
